sections.h2: Who handles your Granville County tax bill
sections.html:
Granville County Tax Administration, at 919-693-4181, is the one number for valuation, relief programs and billing. Almost every question routes there.

A contracted appraiser stands in for the assessor on informal real estate appeals. The next step up, the Board of Equalization and Review, is made up of the county commissioners. The county has five municipalities: Butner, Creedmoor, Oxford, Stem and Stovall. Each town's levy appears on the county bill beside its own line.

Owners outside every municipal boundary, and owners inside Stovall, also pay a fire district tax. That money is restricted to fire protection.

The county rate is 0.631 per $100 of value. A town or fire district rate is added on top, depending on where the parcel sits. Inside a town, add the town rate. In the countryside, or in Stovall, add the fire district rate.

Granville County rates per $100 of value
JurisdictionRate per $100
County rate0.631
Fire service district0.06
City of Oxford0.57
Town of Butner0.42
City of Creedmoor0.58
Town of Stovall0.355
Town of Stem0.35

The county's formula is value times the combined rate, divided by 100. Call the tax office to confirm which districts touch your address, since the boundaries decide which rows apply.

A current-year bill paid between July 1 and August 15 gets 1.5% off. After that, the bill is due September 1, and interest starts once January 5 goes by.

  • July 1 to August 15: 1.5% early payment discount.
  • September 1: standard due date under G.S. 105-360.
  • January 5: last day at face amount.
  • After that: 2% through February 1, then three-fourths of one percent per month or fraction.

You can pay online, by mail, at the counter, through bank bill pay or by phone. E-billing is also available through the county's card vendor, with alerts when a balance, an owner or a due date changes. A mailed check counts by its postmark, so do not wait for the last day.

The next countywide revaluation is set for 2030. Until then, assessed real estate values reflect market conditions on January 1, 2024.

Granville finished a reappraisal in 2018 and first ran on the state's eight-year schedule. In 2020 the Department of Revenue warned that tax values and sale prices were drifting apart, so the commissioners moved to a six-year cycle. Average home sale prices in the county are up 27% since 2021.

A frozen valuation date works two ways. A later market swing, up or down, is not grounds for a different value. A factual error on the parcel record is fair game at any point in the appeal window: wrong acreage, a demolished building still listed, or a structure that was never there.

In a revaluation year the sequence runs like this: notices in January or February, informal appeals February through April, board hearings starting in April, board adjournment in June and a new rate on July 1.

An owner moves through three stages in order: informal review by the assessor, a hearing before the commissioners sitting as the equalization board, and then the state Property Tax Commission.

  • Send in the county's Assessor's Appeal Form early. The appraiser writes back, and accepting the answer ends the matter.
  • If you do not accept it, phone 919-693-4181 and ask for a board hearing. Hearings begin near the end of April and run into early June.
  • Last, give the Property Tax Commission written notice within 30 days of the date the board mailed you its decision (G.S. 105-290).

In years without a revaluation, appeals open January 1 and close the day the board adjourns, never later than early June. Only an owner whose value was changed by a notice sent after adjournment gets extra time.

Personal property runs on its own track. You have 30 days from the first notice to contest, a conference follows, and a written request to the board is due within 30 days after the final answer. Vehicles have a separate county page. A review can leave the number alone, lower it or raise it.

sections.h2: Relief programs that could lower a bill
sections.html:
The state runs three programs, and the tax office at 919-693-4181 can say which one fits. An owner can use only one.

  • G.S. 105-277.1, for seniors and disabled owners: the larger of $25,000 or half of a home's appraised value comes off the tax roll. The 2026 income limit is $38,800.
  • G.S. 105-277.1C, for a disabled veteran: $45,000 of value comes off, whatever the owner's age or income.
  • G.S. 105-277.1B, the circuit breaker: the bill is capped at 4.0% or 5.0% of income, and the difference is deferred as a lien.

Applications use Form AV-9 and go to the county assessor, who must accept them through June 1. If a circuit breaker home sells, the last three fiscal years of deferred tax come due, so tell your closing agent about the program.

An unpaid balance is a lien on the parcel from the January 1 listing date (G.S. 105-355), along with penalties, interest and costs.

Ask Granville County Tax Administration in writing for the amount due on the current bill and for any deferred amount tied to a relief program. Hand both figures to whoever runs your closing.

A balance left alone can end in a court-ordered sale at the courthouse door (G.S. 105-374), though an owner may redeem before confirmation. Paying it off stops the process. The new deed is recorded in Oxford, and the seller pays the state excise tax of $1.00 per $500, or fractional part, before the clerk files it.

A cash sale skips a lender's payoff and appraisal steps, but the tax lien still has to be cleared at or before closing.

sections.h2: Granville County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The county has 61,421 residents and 25,685 housing units. About 77.1% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, and the middle value of an owner's home is $247,700. A household averages 2.52 people.

With roughly one resident in five aged 65 or older (20.0%), the age-based exclusion is worth asking about. These are countywide midpoints, and a specific parcel can sit well away from them.

faqs.q: What is Granville County's county tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is 0.631 per $100 of value. Your town or the fire district adds its own rate on top.

faqs.q: Does paying early save money in Granville County?
faqs.a: Yes. Current-year bills paid from July 1 through August 15 get 1.5% off. The regular due date is September 1.

faqs.q: By when must a Granville County value be challenged?
faqs.a: In a year without revaluation, the deadline is the day the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, no later than early June. Begin with the assessor's form.

faqs.q: Who can claim the $25,000 or half-value exclusion?
faqs.a: A homeowner age 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, who lives in the home and keeps income under the limit, which is $38,800 for 2026. Apply on Form AV-9.

faqs.q: Where is a Granville County deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Register of Deeds in the courthouse at 101 Main Street, Oxford, phone 919-693-6314. The seller pays the excise tax to that office before recording.
